title: Getting started with gristmillr
text: gristmillr needs API key, can create Grist Profile settings. simplest setup two environment variables .Renviron (see usethis::edit_r_environ()): GRIST_SERVER defaults https://docs.getgrist.com. self-hosted site, include team path needed, e.g. http://localhost:8484/o/docs. can also pass key directly, string function looks time (handy keyring): key given string held memory session never saved object, saving handle saveRDS() targets pipeline doesn’t write key disk. Use function form handles persist.
code: GRIST_API_KEY=<your key> GRIST_SERVER=https://myteam.getgrist.com library(gristmillr)  doc <- grist_doc("<doc id>", api_key = \() keyring::key_get("grist"))

title: Getting started with gristmillr
text: grist_doc() accepts document ID URL document, handle remembers server: don’t know ID, list can see: can also create documents grist_doc_create(), returns handle, file grist_doc_import(). reads .grist, .csv, .xlsx .json files guesses column types values: several related tables, see vignette("migrating-data").
code: doc <- grist_doc("https://myteam.getgrist.com/doc/<doc id>") doc grist_orgs() grist_workspaces("current") grist_docs("current")  grist_doc_info(doc) doc <- grist_doc_import("pets.csv", workspace = 1234, name = "Pets")

title: Getting started with gristmillr

title: Getting started with gristmillr
text: convert argument controls Grist cell values become R vectors: "auto" (default) reads table’s column types, Int becomes integer, Date becomes Date, DateTime becomes POSIXct, ChoiceList RefList become list-columns. costs one extra request per call. "basic" simplifies JSON without looking column types. Dates stay numbers (seconds since 1970). "raw" returns API’s values unchanged. Ref columns hold row id record another table. See vignette("joining-tables") resolving joining .

title: Getting started with gristmillr
text: Writes take data frame first return , work pipelines. Data converted way reading: match column rather row id, set . grist_records_upsert() updates records whose values match adds rest. grist_records_insert() adds rows match, grist_records_update() updates rows match. None delete anything, multiple says several records match one row. Grist doesn’t say rows skipped, key-based update needs unmatched = "ignore". Updating id errors row doesn’t exist, default unmatched = "error". Large writes sent chunks. convert = "auto", column doesn’t exist table error, typos surface anything sent.
code: new <- data.frame(name = c("Ann", "Bob"), age = c(31L, 45L))  # The result is `new` with the row IDs Grist assigned in an `id` column added <- new |> grist_records_add(doc, "People")  # Updates match on the `id` column data.frame(id = added$id[[1]], age = 32L) |>   grist_records_update(doc, "People")  added |> grist_records_delete(doc, "People") latest <- data.frame(name = c("Ann", "Cy"), age = c(32L, 28L)) latest |> grist_records_upsert(doc, "People", by = "name") latest |> grist_records_insert(doc, "People", by = "name") latest |> grist_records_update(doc, "People", by = "name", unmatched = "ignore")

title: Joining tables
text: Grist documents SQLite databases, grist_sql() can join server return result. Use table IDs column IDs names. better choice large tables aggregates. SQL results carry column types, dates come back numbers. Convert , use grist_records() types matter.
code: grist_sql(   doc,   "select o.item, o.qty, p.name    from Orders o    left join People p on o.person = p.id    order by o.id" )  grist_sql(   doc,   "select p.name, sum(o.qty) as total    from People p    left join Orders o on o.person = p.id    group by p.id" )

title: Moving data in and out of Grist
text: grist_import() creates table, loads rows, rewrites every reference source key row ID Grist assigned. Tables can loaded order, table may refer . Tables columns named dictionary created types table . grist_import() reads Parquet, CSV JSON files. Parquet source dictionary uses file, otherwise looks <table>.parquet, <table>.csv <table>.json next dictionary (format give). CSV JSON types , values converted types dictionary. number column whole numbers becomes Int, use types = c("Table.column" = "Numeric") Numeric column happens hold whole numbers. columns dictionary imported. column named id isn’t created, Grist row IDs, works key references. names Grist can’t use column IDs changed (column called ID gets ID ID2) keep original name label. function checks everything can changing anything: stops table already exists (unless if_exists = "append") reference points key doesn’t exist (unless orphans = "empty"). request still fails part way, tables rows already created stay document. Three arguments adjust result:
code: new <- grist_doc_create(workspace = 1234, name = "Pets copy") grist_import(new, "pets-export") grist_import(   new,   "pets-export",   # Grist type for a column the dictionary can't describe   types = c("Orders.buddies" = "RefList:People"),   # Which column a reference shows, instead of the row ID   display = c("Orders.person" = "name"),   orphans = "empty" )

title: Moving data in and out of Grist
text: Moving list table another low-code tool needs three steps, second one gristmillr doesn’t . Get table data frame. depends tool. data frames need column identifies row (primary key), columns point tables use keys. Describe tables. Write data frames Parquet (CSV JSON, named table) write data-dict.yaml saying column primary key, columns foreign keys, type column . Import. grist_import() turns foreign keys references. example, take two lists: Projects, ID column Status choice, Tasks, Project lookup column holds project ID, Related lookup holds several project IDs. dictionary can written hand, built R saved yaml12::write_yaml(): Project column relationship, becomes Ref column. data-dict can’t declare foreign key list, Related needs types. target table needs single primary key, values list must keys. importing, data-dict validate-data migration checks files dictionary, including every foreign key value exists table points . data-dict command-line tool separate gristmillr.
code: dir.create("migration") nanoparquet::write_parquet(projects, "migration/Projects.parquet") nanoparquet::write_parquet(tasks, "migration/Tasks.parquet") dict <- list(   `$version` = "0.1.0",   `$learn_more` = "https://data-dict.tidyverse.org/",   tables = list(     list(       name = "Projects",       source = list(parquet = "Projects.parquet"),       columns = list(         list(name = "ID", type = "number(id)", constraints = list("primary_key"),              examples = list(1, 2, 3)),         list(name = "Title", type = "string", examples = list("Roof", "Garden")),         list(name = "Status", type = "enum", values = list("Planning", "Active", "Closed"))       )     ),     list(       name = "Tasks",       source = list(parquet = "Tasks.parquet"),       columns = list(         list(name = "Task", type = "string", examples = list("Order tiles")),         list(name = "Project", type = "number(id)", constraints = list("foreign_key"),              examples = list(1, 2)),         list(name = "Related", type = "list(number(id))", examples = list(1, 2)),         list(name = "Due", type = "date", range = list("2026-01-01", "2026-12-31"))       )     )   ),   relationships = list(     list(join = "Tasks.Project = Projects.ID", cardinality = "many-to-one")   ) ) yaml12::write_yaml(dict, "migration/data-dict.yaml") grist_import(   new,   "migration",   types = c("Tasks.Related" = "RefList:Projects"),   display = c("Tasks.Project" = "Title") )

title: Options for Grist requests, reads and writes — grist-options
text: timeout Request timeout seconds. max_tries Maximum number attempts request fails transient error (HTTP 429 503). user_agent User agent string sent request. Defaults string identifying gristmillr. api_key Grist API key: string, function arguments returns one (e.g. \() keyring::key_get("grist")). NULL, GRIST_API_KEY environment variable used. See Authentication section grist_doc(). hidden TRUE, include hidden columns manualSort. cell_format Format cell values returned Grist. "normal" uses compact values whose meaning depends column type. "typed" returns self-describing tagged values can used convert = "raw". tz Time zone used DateTime columns. NULL, time zone stored column type used, falling back "UTC". col_names Whether name columns returned data frame using Grist column IDs ("id") column labels ("label"). chunk_size Maximum number rows sent single write request. unknown_cols data columns exist Grist table: "error" silently "drop" . checked convert = "auto", modes fetch column metadata. parse TRUE (default), Grist parses string values match type column, e.g. "123" becomes 123 numeric column. FALSE, values stored sent (noparse=true). Values fit column's type never rejected: Grist stores -flags invalid.

title: List, upload and download attachments — grist_attachments
text: doc grist_doc object, document ID document URL. See grist_doc(). filter named list mapping column IDs allowed values, e.g. list(status = c("open", "new")). Rows must match every column. sort Character vector column IDs sort . Prefix column - descending order, e.g. c("status", "-priority"). Use "manualSort" order set Grist interface. limit Maximum number rows return. NULL returns rows. id attachment ID. path grist_attachments_upload(), character vector files upload, uploaded request. grist_attachment_download(), file write, existing directory, case attachment's original file name (reduced base name) used. overwrite Whether replace existing file.

text: Webhooks make Grist send HTTP POST URL records table change. grist_webhooks() lists document's webhooks delivery status. grist_webhook_create() creates webhook. grist_webhook_update() changes webhook. grist_webhook_delete() deletes webhook permanently. grist_webhook_queue_clear() discards undelivered payloads, one webhook whole document.
